## Trial `rootless-container-service-rhel9__q9wedcp`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor deployed a rootless podman container (httpd:alpine) as the unprivileged appsvc user on node1 via a systemd --user quadlet unit, exposed on port 8080, with lingering enabled so it starts at boot without an active login session. Both material outcomes are directly supported by pre- and post-reboot evidence: a full node reboot was performed and observed (distinct boot IDs, brief unreachability, then recovery), after which the service, container, and port-8080 HTTP response were all confirmed healthy while loginctl reported zero sessions and appsvc processes had no controlling TTY. The lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and the addition of the expected 8080 listening socket with no failed services. Hygiene is clean aside from a few small residual log files in /tmp.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.900 | 15/0 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Containerized web application runs as unprivileged appsvc account, serving on port 8080
  - **Why:** appsvc created as uid 1000 non-root user; rootless podman quadlet unit (webapp.container) with PublishPort=8080:80 confirmed running under appsvc's systemd --user instance; podman ps shows container owned by appsvc listening on 0.0.0.0:8080; curl to NODE_IP:8080 returns HTTP 200 with the expected Apache page, both before and after a full node reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ca2a8070985c4ddb`, `cmd-2d81210eb40647f8`, `cmd-7ba325b958944d75`, `cmd-d40d49f6400f4c7c`, `cmd-84b78a90e9104250`, `cmd-f16ede5bc9404364`, `cmd-782543dc98fb43aa`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Service starts at boot while the appsvc account has no active login session
  - **Why:** loginctl enable-linger appsvc set Linger=yes; a bounded reboot was performed with a captured pre-reboot boot_id (6bb7e004...), a reboot acknowledgement, connection loss during the transition, and a distinct post-reboot boot_id (26b9b59d...). After reboot, webapp.service is active, a new container instance auto-started via lingering (4s uptime), HTTP 200 is served on port 8080, loginctl list-sessions reports no sessions, and appsvc processes show TTY '?' (no controlling terminal), directly demonstrating boot-time start without an interactive login both before and after the transition.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-be0ee30e18e1442d`, `cmd-a7c1f5e861b14c19`, `cmd-5c5d4693fcea4e6b`, `cmd-6eeeb84d3d3f485e`, `cmd-9df9acc3f0974021`, `cmd-e06bec0bc8514b3b`, `cmd-58a243d4c1e945c1`, `cmd-782543dc98fb43aa`

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. All executor commands map clearly to installing podman, creating the appsvc user, configuring lingering, writing the quadlet unit, starting/verifying the service, and performing the mandatory reboot verification — no unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found. The only residue is a handful of small log/pid files left in /tmp (podman_install.log, reboot.log, start.log, start.pid), which are low-risk, non-conflicting artifacts of legitimate installation/verification steps rather than abandoned experiments or unsafe exposure.
